grammar.placement: Global options precede `cli`; operation options follow the command path. A rejected global option is an INVOCATION_INVALID error only in the global position; an operation may define its own option of the same name (for example `cli run submit --model`). An operation option or common flag before `cli` (`prose --json cli run list`) is never forwarded to the language: it is an INVOCATION_INVALID error whose suggestedArgv moves it after the command path. In --json and --output json|jsonl every error of a `cli` command line, including an invocation error for a near miss, a misplaced flag or an invalid global, is the openprose.service-operation/1 envelope with the error as `problem`: `operation` is `cli` when the argv names no operation. A bare openprose.runner-error/1 is only for the language and the runner commands (`cli doctor`, `cli harness`, `cli config`, `cli cleanup`).

intentInference.rule: A word or option the grammar does not know is never guessed into execution. The CLI exits 2 with INVOCATION_INVALID, and details.suggestedArgv carries the corrected argv. A synonym from these tables is tried first: the first listed candidate that is a real command or option in that position wins. Otherwise the unique nearest known word is used, by optimal-string-alignment distance (adjacent transpositions count as one edit), within the distance limits below. -h and a trailing help word ask for help. Before `cli`: two words that form a command-path prefix, a complete one-word path, a lone nounSynonyms word that names exactly one command (or a group synonym followed by one of its verbs), a verb before its group (`list jobs`), or a commandRewrites phrase (`stop`, `delete`, `share`, `cron`) are rejected with the `prose cli ...` argv unless a word names an existing file or directory; an optionAliases entry targeting a global option is suggested there too. A word in languageCommands that also names a service command (`status`, `help`, `examples`) is forwarded, and a HOSTED_UNAVAILABLE refusal names the command; under the default hosted harness, which runs no language command, it is rejected with that argv instead. `run FILE` is always forwarded, and its HOSTED_UNAVAILABLE refusal names `cli run submit FILE --preview`. Suggestions are complete: details.suggestedArgv, run as given with details.suggestedStdin (when present) on standard input, is never itself INVOCATION_INVALID. A corrected noun or verb that leaves a command group without a verb gains the group's only verb (`cli models` -> `cli model list`) or becomes the group's --help. commandRewrites map a phrase to a command plus options (`cli run result RUN_ID` -> `cli run show RUN_ID --file outputs/result.json`). optionConversions change units (`--amount 5` -> `--amount-cents 500`); a value that is not a positive whole number is not converted, and the reason states the unit. An unexpected argument fills the one missing required option (`cli wallet topup 500` -> `--amount-cents 500`), except that the argument of an operation with a secretFileOptions option is never echoed: it becomes `OPTION -` with a standard-input example. An unknown option of a --spec-file operation that names a spec key becomes `--spec-file -`, with the JSON object in details.suggestedStdin. An out-of-range whole-number --limit suggests the nearest accepted value. commandAliases are exact spellings of a command (`cli run status RUN_ID` is `cli run show RUN_ID`): they run that command and are not listed in help. optionRemovals name options that are dropped with a reason: the suggestion is the argv without the option (and its value when `value` is true); a non-empty `operations` limits an entry to those operations. An optionAliases target whose value is KEY=VALUE is chosen only for a value that contains `=`. A plural noun names its listing (`cli runs` -> `cli run list`), a verb typed before its noun is swapped (`cli submit run FILE` -> `cli run submit FILE`), and a verb of exactly one group gains that group (`cli watch RUN_ID` -> `cli run watch RUN_ID`). A commandRewrites entry with `argumentOption` passes the typed argument as that option (`cli program run SLUG` -> `cli run submit --from SLUG`). An unknown option with no mapping is removed in the suggestion. An option is matched by distance only when its name without dashes is longer than optionShortWordLength characters or within optionShortWordMax edits, and never to a flag when it was given a value (`--cron x` is not `--json`). An optionAliases target of a paged listing's --before drops a number (pages are cursors: the Action names result.nextBefore), and a DURATION target gains the unit a bare number lacks (`--timeout 30` -> `--wait 30s`). A commandRewrites entry with `argumentCommand` names that command when a positional argument is typed (`cli why RUN_ID` -> `cli run show RUN_ID`); one that appends --help drops the rest of the line; `note` starts the Action. A one-word rewrite followed by a verb of its target's group names that command (`cli schedule list` -> `cli job list`). optionRemovals of `cli job create` (--cron, --every, --interval, --daily, --schedule, --program, and --from) become a schedule spec on standard input: details.suggestedSpec, details.suggestedStdin and `--spec-file - --preview`. optionRemovals of `cli run share` (--with, --to, --user, or an email argument) never hand back a public-link argv: the suggestion drops --yes and adds --preview, and the Action names `cli org invite`. A rejected --output spelling (`--format json`, `-o json`) still prints the error as the JSON envelope. A suggestion that asks for help (`-h` anywhere after a complete command path) is that command's --help alone. A word that holds a whole command line (quoted, so the shell did not split it) is rejected with the split argv.

CANCELLED.meaning: The runner was cancelled before semantic completion.

CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED.meaning: This service operation requires explicit confirmation.

CREDENTIAL_STORE_UNAVAILABLE.meaning: The operating system credential store is unavailable.

EXAMPLE_NOT_VIEWABLE.meaning: This example is published outside the OpenProse service and cannot be shown here.

GITHUB_LINK_REQUIRED.meaning: This operation needs a linked GitHub account on the OpenProse account.

HOSTED_RUN_CANCELLED.meaning: The hosted run was cancelled on the service and will not continue.

HOSTED_RUN_DETACHED.meaning: The client stopped following the hosted run before its outcome arrived; the run was not cancelled.

HOSTED_RUN_FAILED.meaning: The hosted run finished without completing successfully.

INTERNAL_ERROR.meaning: The runner encountered an internal fault.

RUN_SUBMISSION_AMBIGUOUS.meaning: The run submission could not be confirmed and was not repeated.

SERVICE_BALANCE_INSUFFICIENT.meaning: The OpenProse wallet balance is insufficient for this operation.

SERVICE_FEATURE_DISABLED.meaning: This capability is not available for this account.

SERVICE_PREMIUM_MODEL_LOCKED.meaning: This model is a premium model that unlocks with any wallet top-up.

SERVICE_PROTOCOL_INVALID.meaning: The OpenProse service returned an invalid response.

SERVICE_REQUEST_REJECTED.meaning: The OpenProse service rejected the request.

SERVICE_RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND.meaning: The requested OpenProse service resource was not found.

SERVICE_RESPONSE_TOO_LARGE.meaning: The OpenProse service response exceeded the client limit.

SERVICE_WATCH_DEADLINE.meaning: The watch deadline elapsed before the hosted run finished; the run continues.

SERVICE_WRITE_CONFLICT.meaning: The OpenProse service reported a conflicting write.

confirmation.rule: confirm when any request's interaction has agent confirm or never, a route is DELETE, the effect is money, outward or destructive, or the interaction is not reversible; safe GET and HEAD requests never require confirmation; the manifest may only tighten this
confirmation.summaryRule: plannedRequest.summary copies only the listed non-secret top-level JSON body fields (text of 1 to 200 characters without control characters, safe integers, cents as a safe integer that human output also shows in dollars, or the sorted keys of an object); it is omitted when none is present; secrets, program text and input values never appear

routeOverrides.note: program save refines this by the service error text: only 'Sharing requires a linked GitHub login' keeps GITHUB_LINK_REQUIRED; a reserved handle or reassigned slug is SERVICE_REQUEST_REJECTED; anything else, including 'Invalid API key.', is SERVICE_AUTH_REQUIRED.

Only for the duplicate-session 409 (the service's 'This session already has a run.' text with no code) that names no run through X-Run-Id or run_id, after a same-session resubmission or with an explicit --session; after a resubmission any 409 that names no run is also ambiguous. Every other 409 on POST /run is classified by code and status.

featureDisabled.rule: A feature_disabled body is SERVICE_FEATURE_DISABLED whatever the status. details carry only serviceCode and serviceStatus (plus an idempotencyKey already sent); the body's feature name and error text are never copied into the problem or any output.

Print the agent guide: grammar, key precedence, confirmation, exit codes with resume and detach, paging, reading a run's answer and recipes. Makes no request.
Report whether the OpenProse service is reachable and which models you can run. Anonymous.
Diagnose a session in one call: service health, credential, balance, default organization, recent runs, jobs and the next commands to run.

operations.summary: List GitHub repositories reachable through the account's GitHub link.

Report the hold a run reserves: money set aside from the wallet while the run is live. It is not the price. The environment is checked first.
The hold is flat, the same for every program and model, and what the run does not use is released when it settles. A run's price is known only after it settles (`cli run show RUN_ID`, price_cents). The program, inputs and model `cli run submit` takes are accepted, so you can quote the exact command you will submit.

arguments.name: FILE
arguments.description: Program file, or - for standard input, as `cli run submit` takes it. Accepted so a quote names the same command as `cli run submit`; the hold does not depend on it.

options.name: --from
options.description: Run a saved program; a bare SLUG is your own program. @REV is a rev_id, or @N (@revN) for revision N of your own program; without @REV the latest revision is pinned. Accepted so a quote names the same command as `cli run submit`; the hold does not depend on it.

options.name: --input
options.description: Program input; @FILE reads UTF-8 text of at most 1 MiB. Accepted so a quote names the same command as `cli run submit`; the hold does not depend on it.

options.name: --inputs-file
options.description: JSON object of string inputs. Accepted so a quote names the same command as `cli run submit`; the hold does not depend on it.

options.name: --model
options.description: Hosted model id (see `cli model list`). Accepted so a quote names the same command as `cli run submit`; the hold does not depend on it.

options.name: --reasoning-effort
options.description: Reasoning effort supported by the model. Accepted so a quote names the same command as `cli run submit`; the hold does not depend on it.

options.name: --environment
options.description: Execution environment offered by the service (for example builtin or linux).

options.name: --runtime
options.description: Runtime offered by the service. Accepted so a quote names the same command as `cli run submit`; the hold does not depend on it.

options.name: --repo
options.description: Read-only repository context. Accepted so a quote names the same command as `cli run submit`; the hold does not depend on it.

options.name: --commit-output
options.description: Writable repository that receives the run's commit. Accepted so a quote names the same command as `cli run submit`; the hold does not depend on it.

examples: prose cli run quote hello.prose.md --input topic=cats --json

operations.summary:
Run a program on the hosted service and stream it until it finishes, detaches or the deadline passes.
Inputs: --input KEY=VALUE overrides the same key from --inputs-file.
A --wait shorter than the run exits 21 with details.resumeArgv: the run continues, and that command follows it again. Never submit again to resume; that starts a second paid run.

arguments.name: FILE
arguments.description: Program file, or - for standard input. Omit when --from is given.

options.name: --from
options.description: Run a saved program; a bare SLUG is your own program. @REV is a rev_id, or @N (@revN) for revision N of your own program; without @REV the latest revision is pinned.

options.name: --input
options.description: Program input; @FILE reads UTF-8 text of at most 1 MiB. It overrides the same key from --inputs-file.

options.name: --inputs-file
options.description: JSON object of string inputs; an --input of the same key wins.

options.name: --model
options.description: Hosted model id (see `cli model list`).

options.name: --reasoning-effort
options.description: Reasoning effort supported by the model.

options.name: --environment
options.description: Where the run executes (for example builtin: file tools only; linux: a shell without network access). Web access is through the browser:interact tool.

options.name: --runtime
options.description: Runtime offered by the service.

options.name: --repo
options.description: Read-only repository context.

options.name: --commit-output
options.description: Writable repository that receives the run's commit.

options.name: --detach
options.description: Return as soon as the run id is known.

options.name: --wait
options.description: Stop following after this long and exit 21 (for example 90s, 10m, 2h; maximum 6h). The run continues.

options.name: --session
options.description: Use this session UUID instead of a new one (recovery only).

operations.confirmReason: it starts a paid run: a hold (money set aside from the wallet, not the price) is reserved now, and the run's price is charged when it settles

operations.summary: List jobs, the account's job limit and the available job types.
Show one job and its delivery status.

Create a job from a JSON spec. A job starts paid runs on its own, on a schedule or from webhook events, until it is deleted.
Spec keys are snake_case. `type` is required; `cli job list` prints every type with its config_fields. Each type accepts the keys listed under this command's `spec` in `cli service operations --json`; every problem is reported at once.
  Schedule: {"type":"schedule","program_ref":"OWNER/SLUG@REV","interval_seconds":86400}
    interval_seconds 60 to 2678400 (86400 is once a day). The first run starts about one second after the job is created, then one every interval.
    Cron expressions and a time of day are not supported.
    Optional: model, reasoning_effort, environment, inputs (name -> string), files, repository_url, repository_branch, output.
  Webhook: {"type":"webhook","name":"NAME","delivery_mode":"test"}
    optional name, program_ref, receiver, receiver_secret, reply, reply_secret; delivery_mode test or live. Without program_ref it starts no runs: no hold, effect write.
REV is the program's program.rev_id (printed by `cli program save` and `cli program show OWNER/SLUG`), not its commit_id.

options.name: --spec-file
options.description: Job spec: a JSON object of at most 64 KiB (see above), or - for standard input.

requests.when: program_ref is a bare SLUG or names a revision number

operations.confirmReason: the job starts paid runs on its own schedule or events until it is deleted (a webhook with no program starts none until one is attached)

operations.summary:
Change a webhook job's settings. The spec is a partial JSON object with any of name, receiver, receiver_secret, delivery_mode (test or live), reply and reply_secret, for example {"name":"NAME"} (website-change jobs take url, interval_seconds and mode). Any other key is refused locally.
Schedules are refused (SERVICE_REQUEST_REJECTED); change them with `cli job configure JOB_ID --interval-seconds N` or `cli job configure JOB_ID --config-file FILE`.

options.name: --spec-file
options.description: Partial webhook settings: a JSON object of at most 64 KiB, or -.

operations.confirmReason: it changes how a live job receives or answers events; the next delivery uses the new settings

operations.summary:
Replace a schedule job's cadence and run configuration. Schedule jobs only.
Quick form: `cli job configure JOB_ID --interval-seconds N` reads the job and resends its current configuration_revision, revision_token and bindings with the new interval.
Full form: --config-file with the body {"interval_seconds":N,"configuration_revision":R,"revision_token":"T","bindings":[{"program_ref":"OWNER/SLUG@REV","run_configuration":{...}}]}.
Read the current values with `cli job show JOB_ID --json`: status.configuration_revision, status.revision_token (an opaque token), and each status.contracts[] program_ref and run_configuration, under the same names.
run_configuration takes model, environment, reasoning_effort, inputs, files, context_repositories and output as show prints them, except input_entries: move each {name, value} entry into inputs, because every input left out is deleted.
A stale revision_token is SERVICE_WRITE_CONFLICT; while a run of the schedule is in progress the service answers SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE (retry later).

options.name: --config-file
options.description: Schedule configuration: a JSON object of at most 64 KiB (see above), or -. Give exactly one of --config-file and --interval-seconds.

options.name: --interval-seconds
options.description: New interval (60 to 2678400); the current configuration is read and resent unchanged otherwise.

operations.confirmReason: it replaces the schedule's cadence and run configuration; the next scheduled run uses them
